fields.Participants: Corporate Secretary, Policy Owner (department head), Legal Counsel, CHRO, Board
fields.Trigger: New regulation, operational need, audit finding, or periodic policy review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Policy owner identifies need for new or revised policy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Policy owner drafts policy using standard template" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System continuous audit of "Audit Committee approval," (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: Corporate Secretary review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Policy proliferation**: 50+ policies can overwhelm employees; ensure policies are concise and accessible (not buried in dense documents)
- **Acknowledgment fatigue**: Employees signing 50 policies without reading them; focus training on the 10–15 most critical policies
- **Enforcement gap**: Policies without monitoring and consequences are ignored; internal audit should include policy compliance in audit program
System Touchpoints: - Policy management module with version control and approval workflow (W1729.2–4)
- Company-wide policy portal with search and acknowledgment tracking (W1729.5)
- Policy review calendar with automated reminders for 2-year review cycle (W1729.1)
Time Estimate: 4–7 weeks elapsed per occurrence (1–2 weeks + 1 week + 1–2 weeks + 1–2 weeks); cadence-carried steps as authored (Event-driven) — at ~10–15 policy updates/year + 3–5 new policies/year ≈ 13–20 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Policy owner identifies need for new or revised policy: (a) regulatory change (e.g., new BIR regulation, NPC circular), (b) operational incident revealing policy gap, (c) internal audit recommendation, (d) industry best practice adoption, (e) periodic review (all policies reviewed at least every 2 years)

Policy owner drafts policy using standard template: (a) purpose and scope, (b) definitions, (c) policy statement (clear, actionable rules), (d) procedures for implementation, (e) roles and responsibilities, (f) exceptions and approval process, (g) monitoring and enforcement, (h) related documents, (i) version history

Review and consultation: (a) Legal Counsel reviews for legal compliance, (b) CHRO reviews for employee impact and communication plan, (c) affected departments provide feedback, (d) Corporate Secretary reviews for consistency with existing policies

Approval: (a) operational policies: CEO approval, (b) financial policies (procurement, expense, capex): CFO approval, (c) HR policies: CHRO + CEO approval, (d) governance policies: Board or Audit Committee approval, (e) critical policies (code of conduct, anti-fraud, whistleblower): Board approval

Communication and implementation: (a) CHRO distributes to all employees via company portal, (b) training sessions for significant policy changes, (c) acknowledgment collected from all employees (digital signature), (d) effective date clearly stated, (e) previous version archived

fields.Participants: Corporate Secretary, Board Chair, CEO, all directors

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-distribute of "distributes governance self-assessment questionnaire to all directors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "assign owners and timelines for each action" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Courtesy-inflation risk**: directors rate governance generously to avoid friction; mitigated by confidential completion and aggregate-only presentation (steps 2–3)
- **Assessment-without-change risk**: results discussed once and shelved; mitigated by owner-and-timeline action tracking at subsequent board meetings (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Governance self-assessment questionnaire — board composition, meeting effectiveness, oversight quality (step 1)
- Confidential director completion with aggregated results, no individual attribution (steps 2–3)
- Improvement actions with owners and timelines tracked at subsequent meetings (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual self-assessment cycle ~10 days (questionnaire distribution 1 week + director completion and aggregation 1 week + board presentation 1 hour + improvement-action discussion 1–2 hours) ≈ 80 hours/year.

steps.activity: Corporate Secretary distributes governance self-assessment questionnaire to all directors: (a) board composition and independence, (b) board meeting effectiveness, (c) information quality and timeliness, (d) committee functioning, (e) risk oversight, (f) management-board relationship, (g) corporate culture and ethics, (h) director time commitment, (i) board succession planning
Directors complete assessment individually (confidential); Corporate Secretary aggregates results

Corporate Secretary presents aggregate results to Board (no individual attribution): (a) strengths and positive practices, (b) areas for improvement, (c) comparison to prior year (trend), (d) specific recommendations

Board discusses results and agrees on improvement actions: (a) assign owners and timelines for each action, (b) track implementation at subsequent meetings, (c) report to stockholders in annual report (if voluntary disclosure desired)

fields.Frequency: ~20 IC service agreements maintained; annual review
fields.Participants: CFO, Corporate Secretary, Legal Counsel, Transfer Pricing Advisor
fields.Trigger: New service relationship between BuildRight entities; annual renewal
fields.Volume: Core intercompany services: (1) Depot → Logistics: warehousing fees, (2) Depot → Digital Commerce: ecommerce fulfillment fees, (3) Depot → Property Mgmt: lease payments, (4) Holdings → all subsidiaries: management fees

workflows.name: Intercompany Service Agreement Governance, Transfer Pricing & Board Authorization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Logistics → Depot" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Transfer pricing documentation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-file of "filed per W1719" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: CFO review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transfer pricing audit risk**: BIR increasingly scrutinizes intercompany pricing for family-owned corporate groups; documentation must be robust; mitigated by CTL-351 (controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3))
- **Service allocation**: Allocating shared services cost (HQ payroll, IT, finance) across 5 entities requires a fair and consistent allocation key (revenue, headcount, or transaction volume)
- **Billing regularity**: Intercompany fees should be billed monthly (not in lump sums) to avoid period-end distortion
System Touchpoints: - Intercompany service agreement register — warehousing/distribution (Logistics → Depot), ecommerce platform (Digital Commerce → Depot) (step 1)
- External transfer-pricing advisor annual benchmarking study (step 2)
- Agreement updates with board resolutions per W1717, filed per W1719 (step 3)
- Monthly pricing compliance and quarterly intercompany reconciliation per PA-17.2 (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual intercompany agreement review and pricing updates ~1 week; external transfer-pricing documentation over 2–4 weeks/year (advisor-led, ~20–40 internal hours); monthly intercompany recording check within close ≈ 12 hours/year across ~20 IC service agreements.

steps.activity: CFO and Legal Counsel maintain intercompany service agreements: (a) warehousing and distribution services (Logistics → Depot), (b) ecommerce platform services (Digital Commerce → Depot), (c) property lease agreements (Property Management → Depot/Logistics/Digital Commerce), (d) management and shared services (Holdings → all subsidiaries), (e) IT services (Holdings or Depot → all entities), (f) HR and payroll services (Holdings → all entities)

Transfer pricing documentation: (a) engage external transfer pricing advisor for annual study, (b) benchmark intercompany pricing against comparable market rates (arm's length principle), (c) document pricing methodology, comparables, and economic analysis, (d) maintain documentation per BIR Revenue Regulations No. 34-2022 (Philippine TP rules)
Agreements updated with approved pricing; board resolutions authorizing intercompany arrangements per W1717; signed agreements filed per W1719
Monthly: Accounting Manager ensures intercompany transactions are recorded per agreed pricing; quarterly reconciliation per PA-17.2

fields.Frequency: Annual review; ad-hoc updates for organizational changes
fields.Participants: Corporate Secretary, CEO, CFO, all department heads, IT (system configuration)
fields.Trigger: Organizational change, policy review, or new officer appointment

workflows.name: Corporate Signing Authority & Delegation of Authority Matrix

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Corporate Secretary maintains the Delegation of Authority" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve beyond authority" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-review of "review" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: Corporate Secretary review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Config-drift risk**: the DOA matrix is updated but ERP workflows are not, so approvals bypass policy; mitigated by IT configuration change as a controlled step in the same workflow (step 3)
- **Threshold-erosion risk**: inflation renders old thresholds meaningless; mitigated by the annual review with explicit inflation adjustment (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Delegation of Authority matrix — financial approvals by transaction type and value (steps 1–2)
- ERP approval-workflow configuration mirroring the DOA — PO limits, capex workflow per W21 (step 3)
- Annual DOA review — inflation adjustments and organizational changes (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual DOA cycle ~9 days (ERP approval-workflow configuration 1–2 days + CFO/Corporate Secretary review 1 day + matrix distribution and manager training 1 week) ≈ 72 hours/year; matrix maintenance continuous; ad-hoc updates on organizational change.

steps.activity: Corporate Secretary maintains the Delegation of Authority (DOA) matrix: (a) financial approvals: purchase orders, vendor payments, expense reimbursements, capex requests, (b) contractual authority: contract execution, lease signing, vendor agreements, (c) banking authority: account opening, fund transfers, check signing, (d) HR authority: hiring, salary changes, termination, (e) operational authority: inventory adjustments, pricing overrides, markdown approvals

DOA tiers by value: (a) < PHP 50K: Department Manager, (b) PHP 50K–200K: Department Head / VP, (c) PHP 200K–1M: C-Suite member, (d) PHP 1M–10M: CEO, (e) > PHP 10M: Board approval, (f) dual signature for bank transactions > PHP 500K

System configuration: IT configures approval workflows in ERP per DOA matrix: (a) PO approval limits per user role, (b) capex approval workflow per W1811, (c) payment approval limits, (d) contract execution limits, (e) system enforces limits (cannot approve beyond authority)

Annual review: CFO and Corporate Secretary review DOA matrix for appropriateness: (a) adjustments for inflation (thresholds may need increase), (b) changes for new roles or organizational restructuring, (c) board approval for changes to Board-level thresholds
DOA matrix distributed to all managers; training on approval limits; Corporate Secretary maintains signed acknowledgment copies

fields.Participants: Head of Internal Audit, Corporate Secretary, Legal Counsel, HR, accused party's supervisor
fields.Trigger: Annual policy review; report received through ethics channel

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Maintain confidential ethics reporting channel" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "Report received and triaged by Head of Internal Audit" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documented, evidence preserved" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Retaliation risk**: reporters are identified and punished, killing the channel's credibility; mitigated by third-party anonymity and confidentiality discipline (step 1)
- **Triage-burial risk**: reports stall with the implicated party; mitigated by Head of Internal Audit ownership with Audit Committee visibility for high-severity cases (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Outsourced confidential reporting channel — third-party hotline and web portal for anonymity (step 1)
- Report triage and categorization — fraud/theft, harassment, safety, policy violations (step 2)
- Tiered investigation — dedicated/external forensic for high severity with Audit Committee reporting (step 3)
- Resolution and action — disciplinary, legal referral, or closure with reporter feedback (step 4)
Time Estimate: 0.3–4.4 weeks elapsed per occurrence (1 day + 1–30 days); cadence-carried steps as authored (Continuous, Variable, Quarterly) — at Continuous channel availability; ~20–40 reports/year expected ≈ 20–40 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Maintain confidential ethics reporting channel: (a) toll-free hotline (outsourced to third-party provider for anonymity), (b) web-based reporting portal (encrypted, accessible to all 6,762 employees), (c) email to dedicated ethics mailbox, (d) physical drop boxes at each store/DC/HQ, (e) option for anonymous reporting in all channels

Report received and triaged by Head of Internal Audit: (a) categorize: (i) fraud/theft, (ii) harassment/discrimination, (iii) safety violation, (iv) policy violation, (v) conflict of interest, (vi) other, (b) assess severity: high (fraud > PHP 100K, safety risk, senior management involved), medium (policy violation, smaller amounts), low (minor concern, suggestion), (c) assign investigator

Investigation: (a) high severity: dedicated investigator, may engage external forensic team, report to Audit Committee, (b) medium: Internal Audit investigator, 30-day target resolution, (c) low: referred to department head for resolution, (d) all investigations documented, evidence preserved

Resolution and action: (a) substantiated: disciplinary action per HR policy (warning, suspension, termination, legal referral), (b) unsubstantiated: case closed with documentation, (c) reporter protected from retaliation per whistleblower policy, (d) accused party informed of outcome and appeal rights
steps.r: Head of Internal Audit / HR / Legal Counsel

steps.activity: Quarterly report to Audit Committee: (a) number of reports by category and severity, (b) investigation outcomes, (c) action taken, (d) average resolution time, (e) trend analysis, (f) policy or process improvement recommendations

fields.Frequency: Annual disclosure (~315 managers-and-above for full/detailed disclosure; ~6,762 employees for simplified acknowledgment)
fields.Participants: Corporate Secretary, CHRO, all managers and above, Board
fields.Trigger: Annual disclosure requirement; new hire; triggered by specific situation
fields.Volume: ~315 detailed disclosures/year from managers and above; ~6,762 simplified for all employees

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "entertainment received beyond policy limits" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Corporate Secretary reviews disclosures" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documented and tracked" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: Corporate Secretary review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Disclosure-theater risk**: forms signed without honest disclosure; mitigated by materiality review and disciplinary consequence for substantiated undisclosed conflicts (steps 2, 4)
- **Stale-conflict risk**: the annual cycle misses mid-year conflicts (e.g., a new hire's vendor relative); mitigated by triggered disclosure on new situations (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Annual COI disclosure for all managers and above (Store Managers, DC Supervisors, dept heads, C-Suite, directors) (step 1)
- Materiality assessment and mitigation — recusal, divestiture, monitoring (step 2)
- Conflict management plan with annual reassessment (step 3)
- Non-disclosure discipline via employee handbook enforcement (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual disclosure cycle: ~315 manager-and-above detailed disclosures (~15–20 min each ≈ 80–105 hours of employee time) plus ~6,762 simplified acknowledgments; Corporate Secretary review of disclosures over 2–3 weeks ≈ 80–120 hours; conflict-management plans as needed.

steps.activity: Annual conflict of interest disclosure: (a) all managers and above (Store Managers, DC Supervisors, Department Heads, C-Suite, Directors): complete detailed COI questionnaire, (b) all other employees: acknowledge COI policy and report any actual conflicts, (c) questionnaire covers: (i) financial interests in vendors/suppliers/competitors, (ii) employment by or consulting for related entities, (iii) family members in competing or supplying businesses, (iv) outside business interests that may conflict, (v) gifts and entertainment received beyond policy limits

Corporate Secretary reviews disclosures: (a) identified conflicts assessed for materiality, (b) potential mitigation: recusal from related decisions, divestiture of conflicting interest, reassignment of duties, (c) senior management and director conflicts escalated to Board Chair or Audit Committee
Conflict management plan documented and tracked: (a) agreed mitigation measures, (b) monitoring responsibilities, (c) annual reassessment
Non-disclosure consequences: failure to disclose a material conflict of interest is a disciplinary offense per employee handbook; substantiated undisclosed conflicts may result in termination

fields.Frequency: Continuous governance; annual review; event-driven for breaches
fields.Participants: DPO, CIO, Legal Counsel, Corporate Secretary, all department heads
fields.Trigger: Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) compliance requirement; new data processing activity; NPC audit; data breach
fields.Volume: Ongoing compliance for 600,000 customer records + 6,762 employee records + vendor data

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "DPO maintains data privacy governance framework" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-register of "registered with National Privacy Commission" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "checkout, cookie consent, data sharing consent" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: Data Protection Officer (DPO) review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Consent-gap risk**: marketing or profiling without valid consent breaches RA 10173; mitigated by consent capture at activation with purpose-level granularity (step 3)
- **Breach-window risk**: discovery-to-notification exceeds the 72-hour NPC window; mitigated by a rehearsed breach-response runbook with legal and IT on standby (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Privacy governance framework — external privacy policy and internal data protection policy (step 1)
- NPC registration — DPO registration and data processing systems registration (step 2)
- Consent management — loyalty, ecommerce, and profiling consent with purpose granularity (step 3)
- Breach response runbook — 72-hour NPC notification for sensitive personal information (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual privacy audit 1–2 weeks ≈ 40–80 hours/year; privacy framework and NPC registration maintenance annual; consent management continuous (system-supported); breach response event-driven within the 72-hour NPC window per W1203.

steps.activity: DPO maintains data privacy governance framework: (a) privacy policy (external — for customers), (b) data protection policy (internal — for employees), (c) data processing agreements with all third-party service providers, (d) privacy impact assessments for new systems/processes, (e) data retention and disposal schedule, (f) breach notification procedure, (g) consent management for customer data collection
NPC registration: (a) DPO registered with National Privacy Commission (mandatory per RA 10173), (b) data processing systems registered with NPC, (c) annual renewal of registration

Consent management: (a) loyalty program members: consent for data collection, marketing communications, profiling, (b) ecommerce customers: privacy notice at checkout, cookie consent, data sharing consent, (c) employees: consent for processing SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG data, CCTV monitoring, biometric data, (d) vendors: consent for financial data processing

Data breach response (if triggered): (a) within 72 hours: initial assessment, containment, NPC notification (if involving sensitive personal information affecting 100+ data subjects), (b) within 5 days: full breach report to NPC, (c) affected data subjects notified, (d) remedial measures implemented, (e) post-incident review
Annual privacy audit: DPO conducts internal review of data processing practices; findings reported to Audit Committee; corrective actions tracked

fields.Frequency: Annual planning; quarterly activities; event-driven for disaster response
fields.Participants: Corporate Secretary, CEO, CHRO, CMO, affected communities
fields.Trigger: Annual CSR planning (Q4); community engagement events; disaster response needs

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "Annual CSR plan development" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "tracking" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approved by CEO" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-351 (ensure controlled execution — Corporate Policy & Entity Governance (PA-36.3).)
- operational: Corporate Secretary review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **PR-only-CSR risk**: activities chosen for optics without community impact; mitigated by beneficiary and volunteer-hour impact tracking in the CSR report (step 3)
- **Unbounded-commitment risk**: disaster-response spend spirals during emotion-driven moments; mitigated by the CEO/Board approval thresholds (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Annual CSR plan aligned to 200+ community locations — housing/build focus areas (step 1)
- Activity execution — LGU-partnered builds, disaster-response mobilization (step 2)
- CSR reporting — beneficiaries, volunteer hours, donations, linking to VS-25 ESG reporting (step 3)
- Board oversight with approval thresholds — CEO > PHP 1M; Board > PHP 5M (step 4)
Time Estimate: Annual CSR plan development 1 week ≈ 40 hours; ~20–30 CSR activities/year executed quarterly at per-activity scoped effort (community builds, donations per W444, disaster response per W1187); quarterly updates and annual Board presentation.

steps.activity: Annual CSR plan development: (a) aligned to BuildRight's community presence in 200+ locations across the Philippines, (b) focus areas: (i) housing/building assistance (core competency as hardware retailer), (ii) community safety and disaster preparedness, (iii) skills training (construction, DIY workshops for communities), (iv) environmental initiatives (tree planting, waste reduction), (v) employee volunteerism, (c) budget: typically 1–2% of net income

CSR activity execution: (a) community build projects (partner with LGUs for housing materials donation), (b) disaster response (rapid mobilization of building materials for affected communities — Philippines experiences ~20 typhoons/year), (c) skills training workshops (free community DIY clinics at stores), (d) employee volunteer days (1 paid volunteer day per employee per year)

CSR reporting: (a) annual CSR report (may be part of ESG reporting per VS-25), (b) activity tracking: number of beneficiaries, volunteer hours, donations made, (c) budget vs. actual tracking, (d) communication to stakeholders (internal newsletter, social media, community acknowledgment)
Board oversight: CSR activities and budget presented to Board annually; significant disaster response commitments (> PHP 1M) approved by CEO; > PHP 5M reported to Board
